strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with fused local ops
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with all local multiply/divide operations fused between collectives, matching the reference implementation structure. 8 all-reduce dispatches total. Represents the baseline: simple structure with maximum synchronization points but minimal code complexity.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pattern, allowing each rank to compute local scaling on only its shard between phases. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller per-rank computation and potential for better pipeline utilization across the dependent chain.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level aggregation pattern
strategies.desc: Exploit the world_size=224 structure by grouping into subgroups (e.g., 32 groups of 7, or 28 groups of 8), performing intra-group all-reduces followed by inter-group all-reduces for each iteration. Approximately 16 dispatches (2 levels × 8 iterations) with smaller payloads in first level, trading dispatch count for reduced per-collective bandwidth.

strategies.name: Vectorized coefficient broadcast with single scaling
strategies.desc: Precompute the composition of all 8 multiply-divide-reduce cycles analytically, recognizing that repeated (multiply by a[r]/W, sum, divide by a[r]) operations form a pattern. Perform a single all-reduce of scaled inputs and apply the composed transformation locally. Reduces to 1-2 all-reduce dispatches by eliminating iteration dependency through mathematical simplification.

strategies.name: Pipelined reduce-scatter with incremental all-gather
strategies.desc:
Decompose each iteration into reduce-scatter for partial results followed by delayed all-gather, overlapping the reduce-scatter of iteration i+1 with local computation from iteration i. Uses 8 reduce-scatter dispatches followed by 8 all-gather dispatches (16 total) but enables computation-communication overlap by decoupling the reduction from broadcasting phases across iterations.
